claude.sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

links.outcome: Model performance across subgroups of diagnosis, sex and age
links.effect: Model performance differed across subgroups of clinical diagnoses, sex and age.
links.quote: We found model performance to differ across subgroups of clinical diagnoses, sex and age.

links.outcome: Harmful data shifts when transferring models between community and academic hospitals
links.effect: Models trained on community hospitals experienced harmful data shifts on academic hospitals; models trained on academic hospitals transferred well to community hospitals.
links.quote: We found models trained on community hospitals experience harmful data shifts when evaluated on academic hospitals, whereas models trained on academic hospitals transfer well to the community hospitals.

links.outcome: Performance of hospital type-specific transfer learning models versus models using all hospitals
links.effect: Hospital type-specific models using transfer learning performed better than models using all available hospitals.
links.quote: We found hospital type-specific models that leverage transfer learning, perform better than models that use all available hospitals.

links.outcome: Model deterioration from data shifts over time, including during COVID-19
links.effect: Monitoring of data shifts over time identified model deterioration during the COVID-19 pandemic.
links.quote: Furthermore, we monitored data shifts over time and identified model deterioration during the COVID-19 pandemic.

links.outcome: Model performance after continual learning to mitigate temporal data shifts
links.effect: Continual learning was used to mitigate data shifts over time and improve model performance; no numbers reported in abstract.
links.quote: We used continual learning, the process of learning from a continual stream of data in a sequential manner, to mitigate data shifts over time and improve model performance.

unlisted_practices: Diagnosing harmful data shifts without relying on model performance labels

screen.practice: data drift monitoring and continual learning/transfer learning updating
screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates deployment safeguards and practices against dataset shifts across hospitals and over time (e.g., pandemic drift monitoring, continual learning, and transfer learning for site-specific adaptation) for an EHR mortality early warning system.
